Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

# Summary: 2024 UK Political Manifesto

This manifesto presents a comprehensive policy platform centred on "a fair deal" for citizens, addressing five key themes: economy, public services, environment, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economic Proposals

The manifesto prioritises economic stability through responsible fiscal management, investment in renewable energy and home insulation, and repairing trade relationships with European partners. Key proposals include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy to support high streets, creating Lifelong Skills Grants for adult education, expanding apprenticeships, and developing an industrial strategy focused on green technologies and digital sectors.

## Healthcare and Social Care

Healthcare reforms centre on guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases), recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, and improving NHS dental access. Mental health receives significant attention, with proposals for community hubs, school-based mental health professionals, and improved early intervention services. Cancer treatment targets include 100% of patients starting treatment within 62 days of urgent referral.

For social care, the manifesto proposes introducing free personal care (modelled on Scotland's system), establishing a Royal College of Care Workers, and creating a higher minimum wage for care workers. Unpaid carers would receive increased support through expanded Carer's Allowance eligibility and respite break guarantees.

## Environmental Policy

Climate targets include achieving net zero emissions by 2045 and generating 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030. A ten-year home energy upgrade programme would provide free insulation and heat pumps for low-income households. The manifesto addresses water pollution through transforming water companies into public benefit entities and banning executive bonuses until sewage discharges cease.

Nature conservation goals include doubling protected areas, wildlife habitats, species abundance, and woodland cover by 2050, alongside planting 60 million trees annually.

## Education

Education proposals include increased per-pupil funding, clearing school building repair backlogs, and placing qualified mental health professionals in every school. For disadvantaged students, measures include a tutoring guarantee, extended free early years education, and restored maintenance grants for university students.

## Housing and Communities

Housing targets include building 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through garden cities and community-led development. Renter protections would include banning no-fault evictions and creating a national landlord register. Rough sleeping would be addressed through emergency accommodation duties and homelessness reduction strategies.

## Immigration and Asylum

The manifesto proposes replacing hostile environment policies with investment in anti-trafficking measures, transferring work visa policy from the Home Office to relevant departments, and establishing safe legal routes for refugees. Asylum seekers would be permitted to work after three months, and processing targets would be set at three months for most claims.

## Democratic Reform

Electoral reforms include introducing proportional representation through Single Transferable Vote for parliamentary and English council elections, extending voting rights to 16-year-olds, and abolishing voter identification requirements. The House of Lords would be reformed with democratic mandates, and the Ministerial Code would be enshrined in law. A federal approach would strengthen devolution across Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

## International Affairs

Foreign policy priorities include maintaining NATO membership while increasing defence spending toward 2.5% of GDP, supporting Ukraine, and restoring international development spending to 0.7% of national income. The manifesto advocates joining the European Single Market as part of rebuilding European relationships. Middle East policy supports immediate ceasefire in the Israel-Gaza conflict and recognition of Palestinian statehood.

- A legally binding annual cap on migration
- Removal of illegal migrants to deter irregular crossings
- Working internationally to reform asylum treaties

## Defence and Security

- Increasing defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030
- Supporting continued assistance to Ukraine
- Modernising armed forces with emphasis on technology and innovation
- Investing £10 billion in domestic munitions production

## Public Services

Healthcare proposals include increased NHS spending above inflation, recruiting 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors, expanding community diagnostic centres, and improving mental health provision.

## Housing and Infrastructure

The document targets 1.6 million new homes, prioritising brownfield development, maintaining green belt protections, and abolishing stamp duty for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000.

The approach balances net zero commitments with energy security, supporting continued North Sea extraction, nuclear expansion, and renewable investment while opposing immediate transitions that burden households.
